verses.text: The second lot came out for Simeon, even for the tribe of the children of Simeon according to their families. Their inheritance was in the middle of the inheritance of the children of Judah.
They had for their inheritance Beersheba (or Sheba), Moladah,
Hazar Shual, Balah, Ezem,
Eltolad, Bethul, Hormah,
Ziklag, Beth Marcaboth, Hazar Susah,
Beth Lebaoth, and Sharuhen; thirteen cities with their villages;
Ain, Rimmon, Ether, and Ashan; four cities with their villages;
and all the villages that were around these cities to Baalath Beer, Ramah of the South. This is the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Simeon according to their families.

Out of the part of the children of Judah was the inheritance of the children of Simeon; for the portion of the children of Judah was too much for them. Therefore the children of Simeon had inheritance in the middle of their inheritance.
The third lot came up for the children of Zebulun according to their families. The border of their inheritance was to Sarid.
Their border went up westward, even to Maralah, and reached to Dabbesheth. It reached to the brook that is before Jokneam.
It turned from Sarid eastward toward the sunrise to the border of Chisloth Tabor. It went out to Daberath, and went up to Japhia.
From there it passed along eastward to Gath Hepher, to Ethkazin; and it went out at Rimmon which stretches to Neah.
The border turned around it on the north to Hannathon; and it ended at the valley of Iphtah El;
Kattath, Nahalal, Shimron, Idalah, and Bethlehem: twelve cities with their villages.
This is the inheritance of the children of Zebulun according to their families, these cities with their villages.
The fourth lot came out for Issachar, even for the children of Issachar according to their families.
Their border was to Jezreel, Chesulloth, Shunem,
Hapharaim, Shion, Anaharath,
Rabbith, Kishion, Ebez,
Remeth, Engannim, En Haddah, and Beth Pazzez.
The border reached to Tabor, Shahazumah, and Beth Shemesh. Their border ended at the Jordan: sixteen cities with their villages.
This is the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Issachar according to their families, the cities with their villages.
The fifth lot came out for the tribe of the children of Asher according to their families.
Their border was Helkath, Hali, Beten, Achshaph,
Allammelech, Amad, Mishal. It reached to Carmel westward, and to Shihorlibnath.
It turned toward the sunrise to Beth Dagon, and reached to Zebulun, and to the valley of Iphtah El northward to Beth Emek and Neiel. It went out to Cabul on the left hand,
and Ebron, Rehob, Hammon, and Kanah, even to great Sidon.
The border turned to Ramah, to the fortified city of Tyre; and the border turned to Hosah. It ended at the sea by the region of Achzib;
Ummah also, and Aphek, and Rehob: twenty-two cities with their villages.
This is the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Asher according to their families, these cities with their villages.
The sixth lot came out for the children of Naphtali, even for the children of Naphtali according to their families.
Their border was from Heleph, from the oak in Zaanannim, Adami-nekeb, and Jabneel, to Lakkum. It ended at the Jordan.
The border turned westward to Aznoth Tabor, and went out from there to Hukkok. It reached to Zebulun on the south, and reached to Asher on the west, and to Judah at the Jordan toward the sunrise.
The fortified cities were Ziddim, Zer, Hammath, Rakkath, Chinnereth,
Adamah, Ramah, Hazor,
Kedesh, Edrei, En Hazor,
Iron, Migdal El, Horem, Beth Anath, and Beth Shemesh; nineteen cities with their villages.
This is the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Naphtali according to their families, the cities with their villages.
The seventh lot came out for the tribe of the children of Dan according to their families.
The border of their inheritance was Zorah, Eshtaol, Irshemesh,
Shaalabbin, Aijalon, Ithlah,
Elon, Timnah, Ekron,
Eltekeh, Gibbethon, Baalath,
Jehud, Bene Berak, Gath Rimmon,
Me Jarkon, and Rakkon, with the border over against Joppa.

The border of the children of Dan went out beyond them; for the children of Dan went up and fought against Leshem, and took it, and struck it with the edge of the sword, and possessed it, and lived therein, and called Leshem, Dan, after the name of Dan their forefather.
This is the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Dan according to their families, these cities with their villages.
So they finished distributing the land for inheritance by its borders. The children of Israel gave an inheritance to Joshua the son of Nun among them.
According to Yahweh’s commandment, they gave him the city which he asked, even Timnathserah in the hill country of Ephraim; and he built the city, and lived there.

These are the inheritances, which Eleazar the priest, Joshua the son of Nun, and the heads of the fathers’ houses of the tribes of the children of Israel, distributed for inheritance by lot in Shiloh before Yahweh, at the door of the Tent of Meeting. So they finished dividing the land.

footnotes.content: See how God draws lots fairly—Simeon gets their portion, tucked inside Judah's larger inheritance. The Lord doesn't overlook the smaller tribes; He places them exactly where they belong. Even when one family's lot is smaller, His hand is still just.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Beersheba, the well where Abraham once dwelt and where his faith was tested—now Simeon's starting city. Do you see? The land holds memory. God gives His people not just real estate but stories, places where the faithful walked before them.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Hazar Shual, Balah, Ezem—these names are real places for real people. Not grand cities, but home. The Lord knows every plot of ground He assigns and every family who will till it. Simple inheritance is still inheritance.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Eltolad, Bethul, Hormah—Hormah reminds us of Israel's defeat and repentance long before. Now it becomes Simeon's. The Lord redeems even the places of our shame into places of rest. He forgets what we cannot, and gives us new mercy there.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ziklag, Beth Marcaboth, Hazar Susah—the listing feels humble, doesn't it? No grand capital, no famous stronghold. Yet God counts each city precious. He honors faithfulness in small places as much as in mighty ones.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Thirteen cities for Simeon, a full number, a complete provision. The Lord is generous even when the inheritance sits within another's borders. Simeon will dwell among Judah, and this closeness—this too is God's design for His people.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Four more cities—Ain, Rimmon, Ether, Ashan. The Lord adds to what was already full. There's no stinginess in His hand; He multiplies kindness beyond what seemed complete.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The inheritance is gathered up, circled by villages all around, and given to Simeon as their secure home. Notice: the Lord doesn't just mark boundary lines on a map. He ensures each family has a dwelling where they can worship, plant, and rest. This is the shape of His covenant.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Judah's lot was so large it spilled over, so Simeon received their cities from within it. Here's a small mercy you might miss: God adjusts, rebalances, and gives the smaller portion a home among the larger. The strong exist partly to make room for the weak. This is the gospel's shape before the gospel.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Zebulun draws the third lot. One by one, tribe after tribe, God assigns His people to their resting places. The patience of this dividing, the care in it—this is a father's work, not a bureaucrat's shuffle.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The border describes brooks and landmarks, real geography for real walking. Zebulun will know every hill and stream of their land. The Lord doesn't hand out vague titles; He gives His people a place they can come to know deeply.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Eastward toward sunrise, from Sarid through Daberath—the path is marked, the way is clear. There's comfort in knowing exactly where one belongs, in having boundaries that are not prison walls but the lines of home.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The border traces through Gath Hepher to Rimmon. Each name marks a place where God's people will eat, pray, and raise children. The Lord knows each settlement, not as numbers but as homes where His name will be called.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Hannathon, Iphtah El—the borders turn here, loop there. The precision might seem tedious, but it's the detail of love. A parent counts every child's hair; God marks every tribe's boundary. Nothing is neglected.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Bethlehem—yes, a Bethlehem in Zebulun's land, generations before that other Bethlehem in Judah would shine with unexpected glory. The names echo; the Lord works in patterns we only see in hindsight.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Zebulun's inheritance is complete: twelve cities, their villages, their borders. The statement declares finality—this is theirs. The Lord doesn't make promises and then waver; He seals them with land and plenty.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Issachar draws the fourth lot. Each tribe's turn comes in order, no jostling, no anxiety. The Lord's distribution is orderly because He is orderly. His peace flows from the fact that nothing escapes His notice or planning.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jezreel was the future scene of mighty battles and sorrows for Israel. Issachar receives the good land; they will become known as a people who understand the times. The Lord places His tribes in positions where they can flourish and serve His purpose.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Hapharaim, Shion, Anaharath—names that mean little to us now, but to Issachar they mean home, inheritance, future. What is obscure to strangers is precious to those who belong there.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Rabbith, Kishion, Ebez—the list continues, steady as a prayer. Each city is real, each has wells and fields and people. The Lord takes this seriously; so should we.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Remeth, Engannim, En Haddah, Beth Pazzez—the names accumulate like beloved faces in a family. Issachar's inheritance is not sparse; it is full and generous. The Lord knows how to bless.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The border reaches to Tabor and ends at the Jordan—a clear horizon, secure boundaries. Issachar gets sixteen cities and the knowledge that their land is blessed and defensible. Peace comes partly from knowing one's borders.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Issachar's inheritance is declared complete and sure. Each tribe receives not just geography but identity, a place to say 'this is ours' and mean it before God. The Lord establishes His people in tangible, real ways.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Asher draws the fifth lot. The names keep coming, the tribes keep receiving. The Lord's work is thorough; He doesn't rush or skip ahead. Each people matters equally in His sight.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Helkath, Hali, Beten, Achshaph—Asher's cities begin to take shape. These tribes receive what God intends as secure, prosperous homes where they can worship without fear.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Carmel—the mountain where Elijah once called down fire from heaven, now part of Asher's northern border. The Lord assigns His people to lands rich with history and where His mighty acts will one day shine even brighter.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The border turns toward sunrise, loops through valleys and hills. Each turn is marked, each direction is sure. Asher will know exactly where their land ends and their neighbor's begins—this clarity is a gift.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Sidon, great and famous—Asher's border reaches toward the great city. Asher will dwell near the centers of trade and power, their inheritance positioned for both security and blessing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Tyre, the fortified city—names that echo with worldly power. Yet even these strongholds become boundaries for God's people. The kingdoms of men are secondary to God's land distribution. His purpose transcends human pride.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Twenty-two cities for Asher—a generous portion, rich and full. The Lord blesses His people with places that have room to grow, cities where families can prosper and worship freely.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Asher's inheritance is complete. The Lord has been faithful to each tribe in turn. Watch how fair He is, how He sees each people and provides for them. This is the character of God made visible in real estate.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Naphtali draws the sixth lot. Tribe after tribe, the Lord's hand does not falter. Each gets their turn, each receives what the Lord has decided is rightfully theirs. This orderliness is itself a word of grace.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Naphtali's border begins at Heleph, from the oak in Zaanannim. That oak marks a place of remembrance—here God made covenant, or here a judge sat, or here a faithful witness stood. Naphtali inherits land thick with meaning.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The borders turn westward, reaching past Asher and toward the sunrise. Naphtali's land is positioned at the northern edge, close to those who dwell beyond—a people placed where they can see farther than most.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Chinnereth—the sea of Galilee, called by this name in the ancient text. Naphtali receives the fortune of living by living water, a place of abundance and witness where great deeds will one day unfold.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Adamah, Ramah, Hazor—these are Naphtali's cities, their inheritance in a land of hills and waters. The Lord gives His people not just dry land but a place of beauty and resource.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Kedesh, called a city of refuge later—a place where the innocent can flee and find sanctuary in God's law. Naphtali's inheritance includes this holy city, a center of justice and mercy.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Iron, Migdal El, Horem, Beth Anath, Beth Shemesh—nineteen fortified cities for Naphtali. The Lord gives His people security, strongholds where they can worship and rest without constant fear.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Naphtali's portion is complete and declared secure. The Lord has shown steadfast love to the northern tribe as much as to the southern and central ones. None are forgotten, none are slighted.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Dan draws the seventh and final lot among the main tribal allotments. The number seven suggests completion, fullness. The Lord's work of distribution is comprehensive and just.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Zorah, Eshtaol, Irshemesh—Dan's cities begin to form. See how each tribe gets a complete inheritance, bounded and blessed. The Lord does not parcel out the land halfway; He finishes what He starts.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Shaalabbin, Aijalon, Ithlah—Dan's land is in the foothills, positioning them strategically. The Lord places His people not randomly but with wisdom about where they will thrive and serve.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Elon, Timnah, Ekron—each city is real, each will house families who pray and work and raise children in God's sight. The inheritance is not a symbol but a living, breathing home.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Eltekeh, Gibbethon, Baalath—the list lengthens, Dan's portion grows fuller. Even the smallest tribe receives a substantial inheritance; the Lord is generous to all His people.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jehud, Bene Berak, Gath Rimmon—these cities are now Dan's, forever marked as their land. The Lord speaks in deeds as much as words; by giving land, He says 'you are My people, and I am your God.'
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Me Jarkon, Rakkon, with a border over against Joppa—Dan's inheritance reaches toward the coast, a place of trade and connection. The Lord positions His people where they will see the wider world and carry their faith into it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Dan went beyond what was allotted, fought for Leshem, and renamed it Dan—a sign of their strength and hunger for their own name to mark the land. The Lord permits His people to strive and claim their inheritance boldly.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Dan's inheritance is declared complete. The Lord has now given rest and land to every tribe of Israel. No family is left without a home, no tribe without a future. This is the promise fulfilled.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The land is finished dividing. Now Israel turns to their leader, Joshua, and gives him his inheritance among them. The servant of the Lord receives his reward—not taken by force but given in love by the people he led.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Joshua chooses Timnath Serah in Ephraim, builds it, and lives there. The man of God does not demand the greatest city or the richest land; he takes what suits his heart and builds there his rest. This is the mark of a humble servant.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The work is complete. Eleazar the priest, Joshua, and the tribal heads have distributed the land by lot before Yahweh at Shiloh. The inheritance is done, the promise is kept, and the people can dwell in security. This is the rest the Lord promised—not merely absence of war but presence of home.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
